summary: Smart Sand, Inc. (SNDK, NASDAQ Global Select) mines, processes and sells Northern White sand for hydraulic fracturing and industrial uses, with logistics and wellsite services supporting its Wisconsin and Illinois operations. In this Valuatum equity research report dated 7 August 2026, the recommendation is SELL, with a 12-month target price of 1.60 USD against a current price of 2.17 USD, implying -26.3% downside. Market capitalisation is USD 93m and enterprise value is USD 174m. The call reflects projected debt-funded cash burn despite a forecast recovery in EBITDA from USD -8m in 2025 to USD 30m in 2026.

thesis.title: Debt Expansion
thesis.text: Net debt is forecast to rise from USD 81m in 2025 to USD 139m in 2026, a USD 58m deterioration driven by USD 40-52m of annual capex. Even if enterprise value remains near USD 174m, the equity cushion contracts materially, supporting the SELL rating.

thesis.title: Margin Recovery
thesis.text: Sand Mining EBITDA margin must improve from -2.2% in 2025 to 8.1% in 2026 through volume-led fixed-cost absorption, lifting EBITDA to USD 30m. The resulting 5.8x current multiple remains above the 3.4x normalized historical average, making the recovery assumption demanding.

thesis.title: Negative FCF
thesis.text: Free cash flow remains negative at USD 46m in 2025 and USD 54m in 2026 while gross capex stays high. The cash deficit increases leverage and leaves only a 4.5x fair EV/EBITDA multiple, producing a 1.60 USD target despite a 2.17 USD share price.

thesisBreaker: A sharp increase in natural gas drilling, combined with lower rail rates, could quickly reverse free cash flow and materially improve the valuation.

valuePools.name: Sand Mining & Proppant Production
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 307m (98.7%) · Comparable EBIT USD -3m (-100.0%) · EV USD 136m (78.2%)
valuePools.text: Sand Mining & Proppant Production mines, processes and ships Northern White Sand for oil and gas hydraulic fracturing. Its USD 136m EV allocation represents 78.2% of group EV, while modelled revenue of USD 307m represents 98.7% of group revenue and comparable EBIT of USD -3m represents -100.0% of group comparable EBIT. The allocation is roughly half of the approximately USD 260m gross tangible asset base, but current earnings do not support it. The division requires 3.0-3.5m tons annually, delivered pricing above USD 75 per ton and a USD 10-11 per ton cash operating margin; the bridge implies approximately USD 34m standalone EBITDA at a 4.0x multiple. Atlas Energy Solutions produces over 20m tons annually at approximately USD 12.39 per ton, leaving Smart Sand structurally disadvantaged against in-basin supply. Rail-served Bakken and Appalachian demand must stabilise for the allocation to hold.

valuePools.name: Industrial Products & Diversification
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 0m (0.0%) · Comparable EBIT USD 0m (0.0%) · EV USD 24m (13.8%)
valuePools.text: Industrial Products & Diversification covers glass, foundry, filtration and ceramics applications using Northern White Sand reserves. Revenue and comparable EBIT are modelled at USD 0m, while USD 24m of EV, or 13.8% of group EV, represents option value rather than established earnings. The allocation requires 250k-300k tons at USD 40-60 per ton premium ASP and a 15-20% standalone EBITDA margin, implying approximately USD 4m EBITDA at a 6.0x multiple. Covia and U.S. Silica have established technical portfolios, optical sorting and distribution networks, leaving Smart Sand without a clear moat. Dedicated multi-year contracts, local bagging infrastructure and separate disclosure of revenue, volume and gross margin are needed to close the full USD 4m output shortfall. Until then, the allocation remains speculative.

valuePools.name: Logistics, Storage & Wellsite Services
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 9m (2.9%) · Comparable EBIT USD 1m (33.3%) · EV USD 14m (8.0%)
valuePools.text: Logistics, Storage & Wellsite Services, including SmartSystems, is a capital-light recurring service business with modelled revenue of USD 9m and comparable EBIT of USD 1m. Its USD 14m EV allocation equals 8.0% of group EV, compared with 2.9% of group revenue and 33.3% of comparable EBIT. The principal operating issue is declining fleet utilisation as operators increasingly bring last-mile delivery in-house. Its smaller scale means it cannot offset the Sand Mining cash-flow shortfall, although recurring service economics provide some support to the allocation. The division therefore contributes limited diversification while the group funds negative free cash flow and elevated capex.

reverseValuation.intro: The scenario bridge tests how cyclical recovery, industrial adoption and the resulting debt build affect equity value. Revenue is held at USD 365m across the cases, while EBITDA and margin vary with Sand Mining recovery. The primary swing factor is whether operating cash flow can prevent net debt reaching the forecast USD 139m in 2026; the bridge also tests the multiple investors assign to the resulting enterprise value.

coreAnalysis.heading: How the company creates economic value
coreAnalysis.text: Smart Sand creates value by mining, processing and shipping Northern White Sand, principally as proppant for hydraulic fracturing. The model estimates Sand Mining & Proppant Production at USD 307m of revenue and USD -3m of comparable EBIT in 2025, making it the economic centre of a capital-intensive commodity business. Approximately USD 260m of gross tangible assets comprise mines, processing facilities, rail terminals and reserves, but asset value has not translated into positive cash generation at the cycle trough. The division faces cheaper in-basin sand, particularly in the Permian, where operators avoid Class I rail costs despite Northern White Sand’s greater crush strength. Smart Sand’s leased terminals in Ohio and Pennsylvania retain relevance in the Utica and Marcellus shales, but require 3.0-3.5m tons of annual volume, delivered pricing above USD 75 per ton and at least USD 10 per ton of EBITDA margin. Industrial Products & Diversification adds a USD 24m option allocation and could use excess capacity in glass, foundry, filtration and ceramics, but requires 250k-300k tons and multi-year contracts. Logistics, Storage & Wellsite Services contributes USD 9m of revenue and USD 1m of comparable EBIT, yet declining fleet utilisation limits its ability to diversify the group. The SELL rating follows because physical assets remain valuable in theory while current economics and competitive positioning do not yet fund the balance sheet.

coreAnalysis.heading: Putting the divisions back together
coreAnalysis.text: The group bridge turns a potentially defensible enterprise value into a stressed equity case. Revenue is forecast to rise from USD 344m in 2025 to USD 365m in 2026, while EBITDA recovers from USD -8m to USD 30m and reaches USD 44m by 2028. That recovery is absorbed by gross capex of USD 49-52m annually from 2026 to 2028, leaving free cash flow of USD 46m negative in 2025 and USD 54m negative in 2026. Net debt consequently increases from USD 81m in 2025 to USD 139m in 2026 and USD 196m by 2028. Current 2025 earnings support none of the USD 174m EV because EBITDA is negative. A mid-cycle USD 38-40m combined EBITDA at a 4.0-4.5x multiple would support the quoted EV, and the 2027 forecast of USD 37m is close to that requirement. The equity bridge is less forgiving: subtracting USD 139m of projected 2026 net debt from USD 174m of EV leaves USD 35m of implied equity value, roughly USD 0.81 per share. Maintaining the current 2.17 USD share price would require EV above USD 230m. The USD 20m repurchase authorisation adds pressure while cash flow is negative. The target therefore rests on a 4.5x 2026E EBITDA framework and a balance sheet that does not worsen faster than forecast, rather than on current earnings.

coreAnalysis.heading: Scenarios and verdict
coreAnalysis.text: The bull case requires strong Bakken drilling, higher Sand Mining throughput, accelerating industrial customer adoption and sufficient operating cash flow to limit 2026 net debt to USD 120m; it produces USD 2.80 per share and +28.9%. The base case requires the forecast USD 30m EBITDA recovery but accepts the USD 139m debt outcome, resulting in USD 2.14 per share and -1.4%. The bear case requires northern-basin drilling to weaken and the cycle to stall; the resulting USD 20m EBITDA leaves equity effectively eliminated, at USD -0.03 per share and -101.3%. Early evidence will come from quarterly net debt and free cash flow, Ohio and Pennsylvania terminal throughput, Bakken and Appalachian rig counts, and separate Industrial Products revenue and margin disclosure. The central debate is whether Northern White Sand’s reserve quality and industrial diversification can generate enough cash to offset worsening leverage, or whether in-basin substitution and rail costs permanently impair the asset base. Physical assets provide theoretical support, but the balance of evidence is negative: free cash flow remains deeply negative, the recovery is margin-sensitive and the current quote requires EV to rise with debt. That combination supports SELL until pricing, volume and capital discipline visibly reverse the equity squeeze.

risks: Leverage / Equity Squeeze (Sand Mining & Proppant Production): net debt could expand from USD 81m to USD 196m by 2028 and materially reduce the residual equity claim, with quarterly free cash flow versus projected USD 139m 2026 net debt as the early warning - HIGH impact and a thesis-breaker if it occurs.

In-Basin Sand Substitution (Sand Mining & Proppant Production): cheaper regional sand could cap delivered pricing and prevent Smart Sand from passing rail logistics costs to E&P customers, with rail costs and Northern White Sand delivered pricing as the early warning - HIGH impact and structural.

Capital Allocation Misalignment (Logistics, Storage & Wellsite Services): using scarce liquidity for the USD 20m repurchase programme during negative free cash flow could weaken the solvency buffer, with execution of the repurchase programme as the early warning - MEDIUM impact and manageable.

Industrial Pivot Stalls (Industrial Products & Diversification): failure to secure specialised multi-year contracts could prevent margin isolation from oil-and-gas cyclicality, with quarter-on-quarter growth commentary outside oil and gas channels as the early warning - MEDIUM impact and structural.
catalysts: E&P Drilling Activity (near-term, Sand Mining & Proppant Production): stabilisation in Bakken and Appalachian rig counts would support core volume recovery.
Net Debt Trajectory (medium-term, Sand Mining & Proppant Production): keeping full-year 2026 net debt below USD 139m would prevent severe equity-value compression.

Industrial Customer Additions (medium-term, Industrial Products & Diversification): standalone industrial revenue disclosure and high-margin contracts would validate the USD 24m optionality allocation.
Share Repurchase Execution (long-term, Logistics, Storage & Wellsite Services): pausing the USD 20m authorisation would preserve liquidity while free cash flow remains negative.

financials.note: All figures in USD millions unless noted; per-share data in USD.

faqs.q: Is Smart Sand, Inc. a sell in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Smart Sand, Inc. is rated SELL over a 12-month horizon, with a target price of 1.60 USD versus a current price of 2.17 USD and implied downside of -26.3%. The principal issue is not the USD 174m enterprise value against approximately USD 260m of gross tangible assets, but the bridge to equity: net debt is forecast to rise from USD 81m in 2025 to USD 139m in 2026 while free cash flow remains negative at USD 54m.

faqs.q: What is Smart Sand's price target?
faqs.a: The 12-month fundamental price target is 1.60 USD per share, implying -26.3% downside from the 2.17 USD current price. The target uses EV/EBITDA at 80% and an XY scatter ROE/P/BV method at 20%. EV/EBITDA applies a selected 4.5x multiple to 2026E EBITDA of USD 30m, while the XY scatter method implies 2.79 USD per share before the weighted target is set.

faqs.q: Why is Smart Sand rated SELL?
faqs.a: Smart Sand is rated SELL because the expected EBITDA recovery does not prevent balance-sheet deterioration. EBITDA is forecast to improve from USD -8m in 2025 to USD 30m in 2026, but free cash flow remains negative at USD 54m and net debt rises to USD 139m. The company also faces cheaper in-basin sand and rail-cost pressure. Maintaining the 2.17 USD share price would require EV above USD 230m, versus quoted EV of USD 174m.

On the fundamental valuation, Smart Sand is overvalued at 2.17 USD per share. The base scenario produces 2.14 USD per share and -1.4% upside, while the selected target is lower at 1.60 USD because the blended valuation gives substantial weight to a 4.5x 2026E EBITDA framework and projected debt growth. A curve-based ROE/P/BV method implies 2.79 USD, but the company’s negative forecast ROE and cash burn weaken that support.

faqs.q: What is Smart Sand's bear and bull case?
faqs.a: The bear case produces USD -0.03 per share and -101.3% downside if northern-basin drilling weakens and EBITDA reaches only USD 20m at a 4.0x multiple, leaving equity effectively eliminated after debt. The bull case produces USD 2.80 per share and +28.9% if Bakken drilling, Sand Mining volumes and industrial adoption accelerate, EBITDA reaches USD 45m and 2026 net debt is limited to USD 120m.

sources: Primary data: Valuatum Equity Research, Smart Sand, Inc. report dated 7 August 2026 (the value-map allocations, anchor market capitalisation of USD 93m and share price of 2.17 USD).

Competitor context: Atlas Energy Solutions produces approximately 22m tons annually at approximately USD 12.39 per ton; the peer median is 5.0x 2026E EV/EBITDA and 4.6x 2027E EV/EBITDA. Smart Sand’s selected 4.5x fair multiple is below the 5.0x peer median because of smaller scale, geographic concentration and structurally lower margins.

Market data: SNDK, 2.17 USD as of 7 August 2026; the target bridge uses 2026E EBITDA of USD 30m, a selected 4.5x EV/EBITDA multiple at 80% weight and an XY scatter ROE/P/BV value of 2.79 USD per share at 20% weight. Price sources disagree and the 2.17 USD current price should be verified; figures should be independently verified before use.
